capabilities: Edit code files in a Monaco Editor view
Set which file extensions open with the code editor by default
Create new code files from a ribbon button, folder menu, or command palette
Edit individual Markdown code blocks in a Monaco modal that syncs back
Edit CSS snippets from the vault in the Monaco Editor
extras: The README warns that the plugin relies on a hosted version of Monaco Editor and needs an internet connection to work; the author states this dependency may be removed in the future.
problem: Obsidian has no full-featured editor for code files, so code stored in the vault can only be handled as plain text instead of with VS Code-style editing.

relations.evidence: The code editor uses the powerful Monaco Editor, which also powers VS Code.

summary: Monaco-based code editor view that opens code files by file extension, creates new code files, and edits Markdown code blocks and CSS snippets.
